findings.problem: MetricWorkflow uses a flat struct with booleans instead of a typestate enum. Any code can construct MetricWorkflow with is_validated=true and is_sent=true simultaneously, or with neither set, or with conflicting combinations that no domain invariant prevents.
findings.failure_mode: Illegal state combinations are representable and reachable at runtime; the domain has no compile-time guarantee that lifecycle transitions follow a valid sequence.
findings.fix: Replace the flat struct with a typestate enum such as enum MetricWorkflowState { Pending, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } } and make MetricWorkflow carry the enum, so each variant owns only the fields it needs.

findings.problem: status: String allows any arbitrary string value. There is no enum or closed set of status values, so callers can set status to "foo", "", or any invalid string.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid status strings slip through into domain logic; string comparison is fragile and error-prone; no compiler-enforced exhaustiveness when matching on status.
findings.fix: Replace status: String with a domain enum such as enum MetricStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent } and make it the single source of truth for lifecycle state.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool is a standalone lifecycle flag that can be set independently of is_sent, allowing impossible combinations like (is_validated=false, is_sent=true) that violate the domain workflow.
findings.failure_mode: The workflow can reach states where a metric is marked sent but never validated, or validated but in an inconsistent lifecycle position. No transition logic enforces ordering.
findings.fix: Eliminate is_validated as a separate bool; fold it into the typestate enum so that only the Validated and Sent variants carry validated state.

findings.problem: is_sent: bool is a standalone lifecycle flag that can be set without any validation or timestamp, allowing a metric to be marked sent without proof of prior validation or a recorded send time.
findings.failure_mode: Metrics can enter the sent state without passing validation or recording when they were sent, breaking auditability and workflow invariants.
findings.fix: Eliminate is_sent as a separate bool; fold it into the typestate enum so that only the Sent variant exists and it owns sent_at_epoch_ms.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is a standalone optional field outside the typestate. It can be None while is_sent=true, or Some(timestamp) while is_sent=false, creating inconsistent state where sent status and its timestamp are decoupled.
findings.failure_mode: A metric can be marked sent with a None timestamp (lost data) or have a timestamp without being marked sent (dangling state). Both are unrepresentable if sent_at_epoch_ms lives inside the Sent variant.
findings.fix: Move sent_at_epoch_ms into the Sent variant of a typestate enum: Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }, making the timestamp required and co-located with the sent state.

findings.problem: id: String is a bare String used as a domain identifier. Any string, including empty, duplicate, or malformed IDs, can be assigned without validation.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid or empty IDs propagate into domain logic; no compile-time distinction between a metric ID and any other string, enabling accidental misuse in APIs.
findings.fix: Replace with a newtype: pub struct MetricId(String) or pub struct MetricId(#[newtype] u64), with a smart constructor that validates non-empty and returns a typed error.

findings.problem: mark_sent uses raw string literal "sent" to mutate the status field and boolean is_sent=true to mutate lifecycle state. Both parse and boundary are violated: the function sets domain state from unchecked literals without a smart constructor or transition method.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can set the status string to any value and toggle lifecycle booleans directly, bypassing all transition invariants. The parse boundary from literal to domain state has no validation.
findings.fix: Replace mark_sent with a method on the typestate enum (e.g., fn into_sent(self) -> MetricWorkflow) that performs the transition atomically and sets sent_at_epoch_ms from a passed or resolved timestamp.

findings.problem: mark_sent takes and returns a fully mutable MetricWorkflow by value, mutating internal fields in place. This is imperative shell-style mutation masquerading as pure logic. The function name suggests a command but the signature is a data mutator.
findings.failure_mode: No separation between the command (mark_sent) and the state transition; callers can mutate the struct arbitrarily between calling mark_sent and subsequent operations, breaking the functional core boundary.
findings.fix: Make mark_sent a pure function on the typestate enum: fn mark_sent(item: MetricWorkflow) -> Result<MetricWorkflow, MetricError> that returns a new enum variant, or make it a method on an owned typestate struct that returns the post-transition variant.

findings.problem: mark_sent returns MetricWorkflow directly with no Result type. There is no error path for when the transition is invalid (e.g., already sent, not validated).
findings.failure_mode: Invalid transitions are silently no-ops or produce inconsistent state instead of returning a typed error that the caller must handle.
findings.fix: Return Result<MetricWorkflow, MetricWorkflowError> where MetricWorkflowError is a sealed enum with variants like AlreadySent, NotValidated, making invalid transitions a compile-time-enforced error path.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent or any performance claim
no profiler evidence for allocation patterns in MetricWorkflow construction
no allocation evidence for String allocations in id and status fields
no command evidence that cargo fmt/check/clippy/test passes on this crate
no second-ring evidence for any claim about runtime behavior or memory layout
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The struct admits all illegal state combinations at compile time with zero enforcement. Status is an unrestricted String, lifecycle is two independent bools, and sent_at_epoch_ms is a dangling Option. mark_sent provides no validation, no typed errors, and no typestate transitions. Every field is pub, so any external code can mutate state arbitrarily. The crate needs a full typestate enum redesign, newtype ID, smart constructors, typed error taxonomy, and Functional Core / Imperative Shell separation before it can be considered safe.
